thread:
maria.gomez: heads up — I pushed a tiny telemetry toggle to log kernel route signposts for long sequences. trying to repro the seq>512 perf hump. enable with RUNTIME_ROUTE_SIGNPOST=1 on the runtime agent.

ajit: nice. do you have sample logs we can look at?

maria.gomez: pasted a trimmed trace from a canary: 
```
[2026-03-16T17:04:12Z] route: kernel_route=quant_fast_v2 reason=arch_avx2 seq_bucket=256-512 batch_size=4
[2026-03-16T17:04:12Z] exec: p50=12.4ms p95=98.1ms tokens/sec=420 kv_hit=0.93
[2026-03-16T17:06:03Z] route: kernel_route=quant_slow_fallback reason=oom_risk seq_bucket=512-1024 batch_size=1
[2026-03-16T17:06:03Z] exec: p50=28.2ms p95=240.3ms tokens/sec=175 kv_hit=0.65
```

kevin: :eyes: that's a pretty clear throughput drop once the route flips. looks like two issues: kernel slower + kv_hit tanking.

elaine: do we know why kv_hit changed? different key normalization between kernels? or eviction due to smaller batch sizes?

maria.gomez: early hypothesis: the fallback kernel uses a different kv-key sharding (prefix includes quant params) so previously-hot keys no longer match. also batch_size=1 on long sequences means less chance for prefix reuse.

ajit: good call. I'll add telemetry tags for `kernel_variant`, `seq_bucket`, `batch_size`, and `kv_hit` to traces so we can pivot by those dims. shipping a tiny patch now.

maria.gomez: added debug option `RUNTIME_ROUTE_DEBUG=trace` — that prints the selection heuristics (memory estimate, seq_len scoring, priority caps). example config: 
```
runtime_agent:
  env:
    RUNTIME_ROUTE_SIGNPOST: "1"
    RUNTIME_ROUTE_DEBUG: "trace"
    PICK_POLICY: "auto"
```

kevin: short-term mitigation: force `PICK_POLICY=prefer_arc_fast` for the affected fleet to avoid falling back. slightly higher CPU, but keeps p95 reasonable.

maria.gomez: applied canary with prefer_arc_fast; p95 improved back to ~110ms in the canary. still slightly higher CPU but acceptable for customer-facing traffic.

ops-bot: deploy canary -> us-west-2 (job #4921) succeeded. :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: scheduled perf-sweep for seq=[128,256,512,768,1024] for that canary. will post results.

maria.gomez: next actionable items: 1) add kernel_variant tags (done by ajit), 2) audit kv key derivation in quant_slow_fallback, 3) rework batching heuristic to avoid tiny batches for long seqs (prefer aggregate length cap). filing follow-up.

kevin: create an issue and tag eng-runtime; I'll own triage and prioritization.

maria.gomez: created issue #845: "kernel-route: seq>512 fallback causes kv miss and p95 regression" https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/845

ajit: small note — when we log signposts, include `reason_score` (numeric) so we can threshold in queries instead of parsing reason strings.

elaine: agreed. also capture `mem_est_mb` and `est_tokens_per_gpu` in signpost logs. helps explain why the heuristic picked the fallback.

ci-bot: perf-run complete. summary csv: https://internal.ci/runs/4921.csv 
results: seq=256 tokens/sec=430, seq=512 tokens/sec=410, seq=768 tokens/sec=190, seq=1024 tokens/sec=180.

maria.gomez: thanks — that CSV matches the signpost logs. will attach to the issue and start the kernel patch review. :pray:
